# S26 - Test this workflow

The designer can test a saved draft with a sample request and explicit scenarios for approvals, calls, child outcomes and messages. The compiler evaluates the canonical definition without starting an engine process, creating tasks, sending notifications, invoking connectors or storing request values. The catalog endpoint checks workflow.read visibility and a draft revision; validation blockers and invalid form values stop evaluation. Audit records contain counts only.

Playback explains decisions, chosen routes, simulated calls, approvals, skipped waits, message arrival/timeouts, parallel branches and child repetitions. Rule and route coverage identify what the case did not exercise. Simple, medium and complex fixtures are shared between Java and mock goldens under `examples/fixtures/simulation/`. Optional child-definition simulation uses active released definitions; it does not claim real engine timing or concurrent ordering.

Bounds are enforced: 64 KiB input/scenario API documents, 64 KiB scenario parsing, 400 steps per workflow and 1,000 steps shared across nested children, 25 actual child simulations across the whole tree, three nested child levels, 100 settings per scenario group, 25 supplied child outcomes, and at most 25 child definitions loaded from the catalog. Budget exhaustion produces needsAttention with TEST_LIMIT evidence. The rate limiter allows 30 requests per minute per person per pod, evicts inactive identities and caps active identity tracking at 10,000.

Named cases remain in this browser, keyed by signed-in subject, workspace and workflow. Old unscoped storage is ignored rather than copied into another person's session. Up to ten cases can be saved, each at most 64 KiB with scalar arrays bounded to 25 items. Import/export is explicit: imports are capped at 1 MiB and 100 candidates, reject unsupported versions, and skip malformed cases. Exported files contain sample inputs and scenarios; use appropriate sample data. Cases are not server shared or scheduled regression jobs.

Evidence: WorkflowSimulatorTest and WorkflowSimulatorGoldenTest cover canonical evaluation and nested budgets; SimulationApiTest checks visibility, revision and absence of runtime side effects; SimulationLimiterTest checks window and identity bounds. Frontend savedCases, TestPanel, scenario model and mock simulator tests verify playback, outcomes, bounds and cross-subject isolation. Root coordinates the final Java/integrated build; passing status belongs in the central tracker after execution.

Limits: simulation is deterministic guidance, not the workflow engine. It skips time, substitutes connector answers and executes parallel branches in deterministic order. It cannot prove network behavior, engine recovery or real parallel races; those remain runtime integration tests.
